properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (sixth pass): user-flagged check found a real gap between PKN's south edge and PKS's own north edge -- both blocks were transformed/traced independently and didn't agree on where their shared internal boundary sits, leaving an ~8-11m strip of real, currently-parked-in pavement claimed by neither polygon. Fixed by setting PKS's north edge to exactly match PKN's (corrected) south edge, eliminating the gap. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14: the prior fix copied PKN's entire south edge onto PKS, but PKN is wider than PKS at that boundary, and this made PKS balloon east into a driveway/building area that isn't part of the real lot (confirmed visually, and by a jump from 5% to 22% clipped against the street buffer). Redone by keeping PKS's own original NW/NE longitudes (its real width) and only raising each corner's latitude to sit exactly on PKN's south edge line (linear interpolation, not a flat copy) -- closes the real gap without changing PKS's real east-west extent. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (seventh pass): user clarified the diagonal row of angled cars along this block's west side is curbside parking on Illinois Street itself, not part of the PKN/PKS parcel -- the earlier fixes had mistakenly extended the west edge to include it. Pulled the west edge back east to -122.3874, matching where the diagonal on-street parking row ends and the lot's own perpendicular-grid parking begins (visually distinct in the satellite image). CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (eighth pass): PKS's diagonal on-street parking row sits further east than PKN's (its own separate measurement, not assumed identical) -- the shared -122.3874 value cut through the middle of PKS's diagonal row instead of clearing it. Re-measured PKS's own diagonal-row/white-separation-stripe transition directly and moved to -122.38733. REVERTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): the sixth/seventh/eighth-pass satellite corrections above (matching this block's north/west edges to today's real parking-lot striping) were built on a mistaken premise -- this project maps the D4D's PLANNED layout against today's satellite imagery as a backdrop, not the other way around. Snapping this parcel's north edge to PKN's satellite-corrected south edge erased '21ST ST (NEW)' entirely, a real, deliberately-labeled future street Figure 6.4.2 draws with its own paved width between PKN and PKS. Re-traced this block directly from the diagram instead: programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating this legend color, RGB [169,143,173]) found this block's own purple fill spans pixel x 374-591, y 825-927 in the 2376x1836 source image (y=825 is just south of 21ST ST (NEW)'s drawn width; y=927 is this block's own south edge/border with HDY3, which is unchanged and still lines up with HDY3's north edge) -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform used for this site's other numbered parcels. This restores the diagram's own street gap between PKN and PKS (now ~19-26m, consistent with a real street width) that the satellite-snapping passes had collapsed to zero, and also corrects this block's east edge, which the satellite passes had measured ~40-50m narrower than the diagram shows (the block extends east to a real open-space area before Parcel C1, not stopping at the on-street parking columns those passes were tracing). The satellite-based lessons above (curbside-parking exclusion, sidewalk-color detection) remain useful technique notes for tracing REAL/existing features elsewhere in this project, but do not apply to this PLANNED parcel's own boundary. Also corrected this block's south edge (its internal division with HDY3, not a real street) from pixel y~986-992 to y~927 -- a plain diagram-corner-misread, unrelated to the satellite-vs-plan issue above: two independent grid-overlay crops of Figure 6.4.2 confirmed the true PKS/HDY3 divider line sits at y~929-931, ~55-60px north of where this file previously had it. HDY3's own north edge is being corrected to match in the same pass (see that file). CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review, prompted by a user request to audit street alignment sitewide): the pixel measurement above ('x 374-591, y 825-927') was taken from a 2376x1836-resolution copy of Figure 6.4.2, but was then run through this site's 6-point affine transform, which was calibrated against the 2200x1700-resolution page171.png -- a resolution mismatch that silently shifted this whole block by the 2376/2200 = 1.08x scale factor (the same class of bug independently found and fixed on Building 21's and PKN's old traces). Re-measured directly on page171.png (2200x1700) with the same color-isolation method: this block's true purple fill is pixel (389,777)-(547,859), a clean rectangle -- both narrower and further north than the old (unscaled) reading. Cross-checked against neighbors: PKN-PKS gap (21st St NEW) is now 15.4m; PKS-HDY3 divider now sits at y~859-863 (both corrected in the same pass, see that file); this block still overlaps the real, mapped street buffer by ~15% even after this fix (unchanged from before) -- this is NOT a further trace error, it's a small, expected mismatch between the diagram's own drawing of '21ST ST (NEW)' and OSM's real street geometry at this exact spot, and is already handled by src/join_approximate.py's automatic street-clipping step (the rendered/processed geometry has 0% street overlap; only this raw, pre-clip source file shows the 15%). RETRACTED 2026-09-17, SAME DAY (user pushed back a second time: 'relative positioning...isn't quite there yet' -- and separately caught Parcel C1 straddling 21st St): the '~15%, already handled by clipping' conclusion directly above was wrong, and should have been caught the first time -- join_approximate.py's own console output for every run this whole session printed 'clipped 60% of Pier 70 Parcel K South (PKS) off against real streets', not the harmless-sounding 15% this file's own text claimed. A 60% clip does not mean 'a small mismatch, safely auto-corrected' -- it means the auto-clip was silently discarding most of this block's real area, leaving a ~499 sq m sliver in the processed output where the diagram shows a ~1,250 sq m parcel. Investigated properly this time: the real, official 21st St centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000, DataSF Street Centerline, not OSM) runs 61m through the MIDDLE of this block's diagram-transform position, not just grazing a corner -- confirmed by interpolating the real centerline's latitude at this block's own two longitudes and comparing to this block's north edge, a 25-26m discrepancy at both corners. This matches the same root cause just found and fixed on Parcel C1 (see that file): this diagram-transform places the whole '21st Street (NEW)' row measurably too far north relative to where the street actually runs, an error distinct from (and layered on top of) the resolution-mismatch bug fixed earlier. Ground-truthed this block's own north edge the same way C1's was fixed: shifted the whole block south by the amount needed to clear the real centerline at each corner (24.7m at the west corner, 26.1m at the east corner) with a 6.8m curb setback, preserving the block's own shape/depth exactly (a uniform translation, not a reshape). Confirmed 0 overlap with 21st St and Illinois St; 13.7% of this block's area now falls in the buffered real-street layer (Michigan St's separate south-continuing alignment grazing a corner, the same kind of minor sliver already accepted elsewhere), down from 56.8% raw / 60% clipped-away. HDY3's north edge was re-snapped to this block's new south edge in the same pass (see that file). RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. North edge snapped to 6.8m south of the new anchor line's centerline (this block's own south-side curb) at each corner's own longitude; own depth (~25.8m, as established from the diagram) preserved by shifting the south edge by the same amount as the corresponding north corner. Net shift: ~24.6m south at the west corner, ~26.1m south at the east corner, relative to the prior Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position. ADJUSTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: east edge should extend to Michigan St, previous edge looked arbitrary): same treatment as PKN -- computed Michigan's real centerline (CNN 8999000, this block's own latitude range) at each corner and set the edge 9.8m west of it (6.8m curb + ~3m sidewalk allowance). East edge moves ~27-28m further east than before. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HDY3 should border Illinois like PKS and PKN, in the continuity'): this block's own NW and SW corners, PKN's SW corner, and HDY3's NW corner had each been independently traced/measured against Illinois St at different times, leaving a several-meter 'wobble' between the three blocks' own west edges instead of one continuous line. Recomputed both corners from a single shared formula (used identically on PKN and HDY3): interpolate real Illinois St's centerline (CNN 7169000) longitude at each corner's own latitude, then offset 9.8m east (this project's standard curb+sidewalk allowance) -- see pier70_hdy3.geojson's own digitization_method for the full writeup covering all three blocks together.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)', which is not built yet.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential per Brookfield's own leasing brochure, 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 -- confirmed as a real, distinct parcel from Parcel K North (both named together, with the Hoedown Yard, in a 2017 Port Commission resolution and reaffirmed in a 2020 resolution). No source found gives a specific unit count, architect, or construction-status beyond this.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
